title: Prime-to-p finite trace: norm and Frobenius error bound
statement: Let $F\subseteq E$ be complete fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values: $|x|=0$ iff $x=0$, $|xy|=|x||y|$, $|1|=1$ and $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$. Put $F^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] and $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$, and let $p=\operatorname{char}\widetilde F>0$. Assume $E/F$ is finite Galois of degree $n$ with $p\nmid n$; here Galois means normal and separable, normal means every irreducible polynomial over $F$ with a root in $E$ splits over $E$, and separable means the minimal polynomial of each element has distinct roots. Define $\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(x)$ as the trace of the $F$-linear endomorphism $y\mapsto xy$ of $E$ and put $T(x)=n^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(x)$, where $n$ denotes its nonzero image in $F$. Then $T:E\to F$ is $F$-linear, $T(c)=c$ for every $c\in F$, and for every $x\in E$ one has $$|T(x)|\le|x|,\qquad |T(x^p)-T(x)^p|\le |p|\,|x|^p.$$ The integer $p$ in $|p|$ denotes its image in $F$, so the second right-hand side is zero when $\operatorname{char}F=p$.

source.place: Agent-supplied averaging-of-conjugates estimate for the coefficient-normalization supplement to Temkin Proposition 6.2.4, proof, printed p. 47; this estimate is not stated as a theorem of Temkin. The contextual primary source was read at https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS2; local archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Every natural integer has absolute value at most one, by induction using the ultrametric inequality and $|1|=1$. The residue of $n$ in $\widetilde F$ is nonzero, since that field has characteristic $p$ and $p\nmid n$. Thus $|n|=1$, so $n\ne0$ and $|n^{-1}|=1$. Compatibility of absolute values gives an injection $\widetilde F\hookrightarrow\widetilde E$: the map on unit balls has kernel exactly $\{a\in F:|a|<1\}$. Therefore $\operatorname{char}\widetilde E=p$ as well. These quotients are fields: an element of the unit ball has nonzero residue precisely when its norm is one, in which case its inverse also belongs to the unit ball. Also $n\ge1$, since $E$ contains its nonzero unit.

proof.text: Choose an $F$-basis of $E$ with $n$ elements and let $M_x$ be the matrix of multiplication by $x$. Then $M_{x+y}=M_x+M_y$ and $M_{cx}=cM_x$ for $c\in F$. Summing diagonal entries proves that $x\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(x)$, hence $T$, is $F$-linear. For $c\in F$, $M_c=cI_n$, so $\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(c)=nc$ and $T(c)=c$. This uses the definition of the trace of a finite-dimensional endomorphism, not an identification with Mathlib's characteristic-zero normalized trace.

proof.text: Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)$. For $\sigma\in G$, the absolute values $u(z)=|z|$ and $v(z)=|\sigma(z)|$ both restrict to $|\cdot|_F$. The extension is algebraic: for each $z$, the $n+1$ vectors $1,z,\ldots,z^n$ are linearly dependent. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-absolute-value-unique], with complete nontrivially valued base $F$, to obtain $|\sigma(z)|=|z|$ for all $z$.

source.place: spectralNorm_unique_field_norm_ext, lines 770-773, applied to the two extending absolute values.

proof.text: The group $G$ is finite by [lem-trf-galois-trace-sum] and nonempty because it contains the identity. Write $S=\sum_{\sigma\in G}\sigma(x)$ and $U=\sum_{\sigma\in G}\sigma(x^p)$. The same node identifies $S=\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(x)$ and $U=\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(x^p)$ inside $E$. By [lem-trf-nonarchimedean-finite-sums] and step 3, $|S|\le\max_\sigma|\sigma(x)|=|x|$. Step 1 and compatibility on $F$ give $|T(x)|=|n^{-1}S|\le|x|$.

source.place: trace_eq_sum_automorphisms, lines 263-272, followed by Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/IsNonarchimedean.lean, apply_sum_le_sup, lines 134-137.

proof.text: Apply the first inequality of [lem-trf-nonarchimedean-prime-power-root-estimates] in $E$ with exponent $q=p^1=p$ and the nonempty family $(\sigma(x))_{\sigma\in G}$. Its residue-characteristic hypothesis was checked in step 1. Automorphisms preserve powers, so $\sum_\sigma\sigma(x)^p=U$; step 3 yields $|S^p-U|\le |p|\,|x|^p$. Apply that same first inequality in $F$ to the $n\ge1$ copies of $1$, again with $q=p$, to get $|n^p-n|\le |p|$. Since $|n|=1$, the identity $n^{p-1}-1=(n^p-n)/n$ gives $|n^{p-1}-1|\le|p|$. No assertion about roots from the cited node is used.

source.place: Agent-supplied normalized-trace supplement to Proposition 6.2.4; elementary assembly using Lemma 6.2.10(i), printed p.46; primary text read at https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS2 on 2026-10-24; archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Inside $E$ the exact algebraic identity is $$T(x^p)-T(x)^p=n^{-p}(U-S^p)+n^{-1}(1-n^{1-p})U.$$ Step 4 applied to $x^p$ gives $|U|\le|x^p|=|x|^p$. Moreover $|n^{-p}|=|n^{-1}|=1$ and $|1-n^{1-p}|=|n^{p-1}-1|\le|p|$ by steps 1 and 5. Each of the two displayed summands consequently has absolute value at most $|p|\,|x|^p$. The two-term ultrametric inequality gives the desired bound, also in $F$ by compatibility. When $\operatorname{char}F=p$, this upper bound is zero and gives the asserted exact equality.
